#1369. Slow and dull Man Utd are just not good enough

Manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet. You fix one problem – being far too vulnerable to conceding goals – only to create another – lacking the threat to score. It is all very Meh United not Man United. The indisputable fact is they are just not very entertaining to watch. They are slow and dull.

In the end it also points to another thing. The thing highlighted in midweek by Lisandro Martínez after the Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid: they do not have the strength in depth to compete.

What they do have appears to not be fit for purpose. Certainly Michael Carrick, the under-pressure manager, is struggling to get the best out of the resources he has.

“It’s like a duvet,” Toshack, the former Real Madrid and Wales manager, famously said of football. “If you pull it up, your feet get cold. If you pull it down, your shoulders get cold.”

There will have been times in the last few days, with the intense criticism and scrutiny over his future, when Carrick will have simply felt like dragging that duvet up over his head and keeping it there.

Defeat by Leeds United would have been unthinkable. It would have put Carrick under potentially intolerable pressure in what appears to be a pivotal week, with Como away in the Champions League and a home Premier League fixture against Bournemouth in the coming days.

Was this a lifeline or the tightening of the noose for Carrick? Time will soon tell. The relief of avoiding defeat was tempered by the reality of it now being just one win in their opening seven league games – at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town – and they are down in 13th place. It is six games without a win in all competitions.

That is unacceptable and is their fewest number of league victories in a top-flight campaign since 1986-87. Back then they sacked their manager in November and brought in a certain Alex Ferguson.

The hard truth is Carrick needs to start collecting some “Ws” in those results columns. United are already 14 points behind leaders Manchester City and five outside the probable Champions League places. Qualifying again for that tournament must be the minimum expectation.

Ruben Amorim, Carrick’s predecessor, lost his job within 24 hours of the same 1-1 scoreline at Elland Road last season – dismissed after Martínez-like explosive comments again aimed at director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick will not suffer the same fate after this, but the ice is becoming increasingly thin.

We have seen this movie before at United. A slow start to the season, a period of drift, falling out of contention, no reaction on the pitch, backing from the hierarchy that becomes increasingly unconvincing. And then a change.

Can Carrick, who genuinely does still retain support at the highest level, alter that pattern? Does he have it in him? Is he too passive like his team? Carrick said this draw felt like a “fresh start”, but on this evidence that comment can be classified as wildly optimistic.

Having directed his criticism at the United hierarchy, and specifically Wilcox, the former Leeds winger who was here, over a lack of summer signings, Martínez apologised and was named in the starting XI. But the Argentine only lasted to half-time, withdrawn injured with a tight thigh, and sat watching the second half with his hood up over his head.

What United did sign in the last window was three midfielders – at a cost of £155m – and all three started: Carlos Baleba alongside Andrey Santos with Youri Tielemans in the No 10 role, which meant Bruno Fernandes was pushed out to the left, from where he constantly wanted to come in-field, with Amad Diallo on the right.

Carrick talked of having a “fresh spine” as well as that fresh start. But it did not make for a potent combination even if, further forward, Bryan Mbeumo played through the middle and scored one. He should have scored another.

Bryan Mbeumo finds the net this time to put Manchester United 1-0 up at Leeds! 🔴 https://t.co/NKDIhlUND1

But beyond that United created little. “It was a dominant performance against Man United,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, claimed. He was right. If one team deserved to win it was his. They had the chances but snatched at them with Anton Stach, in injury time, having a weak shot cleared off the line by Martínez’s replacement Noussair Mazraoui after a mistake by goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Stach had to score.

United were ahead at half-time. Mbeumo had headed wastefully wide when unmarked but did well to force his way past James Justin and meet a low cross from Tielemans to poke the ball home. The way the usually undemonstrative Carrick punched the air in his technical area showed the pressure he felt. It was something to build on. To gain control.

Leeds had started well but did not really pose much of a threat – beyond forcing Lammens to save well from Nico Elvedi’s downward header – and maybe the earlier kick-off subdued the crowd. This was far from a bear pit.

But after the break, Leeds were comfortably the better side. The nature of their equalising goal, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin too strong and alert for first Baleba and then Mbeumo to fire in from a corner, exposed the enduring softness at the heart of United.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalises for Leeds against Manchester United 👊 https://t.co/mnpyxZJKbm

And that must be addressed by Carrick, especially as he appeared to sacrifice attacking intent by shoring up defensively. But that duvet is looking far too inadequate right now. Or Carrick is making it appear so.

Michael Carrick says he has put on “the headphones” this week in an effort to drown out the noise, but admitted Manchester United have to stop their struggles from snowballing.

United sit just two points above the relegation zone after a 1-1 draw at Leeds left them with just one win from their opening seven Premier League matches.

Carrick claimed the result felt like a “fresh start” after a week in which Lisandro Martínez publicly apologised for criticising Jason Wilcox, the United director of football, and the Old Trafford board.

But the United manager acknowledged their position “doesn’t look too good” and that they must start winning soon to stop the club from entering another doom cycle.

“Listen, we’re not accepting it as everything’s great by any stretch, so I’m realistic with that,” said the United manager, who claimed “the headphones have been on this week”.

“But sometimes you do struggle, sometimes there’s a bit of it where you have to find a way through it. We haven’t really had to go through that yet [before now] and we have to find a way through it.

“There has been a cycle at times here over a period of time when it can go in different directions. We’ve got to be stable enough to keep doing the right things for the right reasons as a group, and we’re more than capable of winning football matches.

“I understand the situation doesn’t look too good if you look at it from a certain way, but I’ve no doubts we can go on a good run.”

United face Como in the Champions League in Italy on Wednesday before Bournemouth visit Old Trafford four days later.

Carrick said he remains convinced United can still have a strong campaign, despite their worst start to a season for 40 years. I know what we’ve got in the changing room, where we want to get to, how we want to get there,” he said. “We know we can do it.

“We’ve done it for some time, and we feel we’re a better group now, and I do feel that. Sometimes it doesn’t always show, but you get a feeling and I’m encouraged by a lot of things. And if we keep doing the right things, I think we can still have a really good season.”

Asked if he would be putting the headphones back on this week ahead of two more pivotal games, Carrick added: “Nah, it’s always quiet for me.”

Martínez was substituted at half-time at Elland Road with a tight thigh just days after his tirade at club executives and Marcus Rashford was left out for “purely tactical” reasons. “Nothing personal, the front players were doing a good job on and off the ball,” Carrick said. “Everyone is ready for Wednesday.”

The Leeds boss told Sky Sports: “We are slightly disappointed it is just a point. Overall, I felt it was not necessary to be losing at half time but it is still Manchester United. Second half, we got the equaliser, we should have kept up the dominance, too many strikes went over the crossbar but it was overall a solid performance. We should have won the game but we move on.

“We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month if we were seen as favourites against Manchester Untiedbut we have earned this. We wanted to prove the comments right.

“We were the dominant side but we couldn’t capitalise as we lacked quality in and around the box.

“It says a lot about how much respect we have earned. Overall, this is where we are at the moment and overall, it is a good place to be.

“It is still difficult in this league to win points. You have to be clinical and be very, very effective but we have to keep going.”

Speaking to Sky Sports, he said: “I think we could’ve played with a bit more quality in the final third, particularly in the first half. We were getting good quality in the box but just not enough numbers.

“We made sure in the second half we came out with more confidence going forward. I think we were unlucky not to win the game.

“They tried to [match us up formation-wise]. Not surprised given what happened last season. They were probably looking at our physical output and the way we liked to play and tried to go man-for-man.

“It took us a little bit to adjust to it, but I don’t think it was too difficult to adjust. It was more down to us and maybe a lack of quality in the final third.”

Brighton & Hove Albion 5 Crystal Palace 0

It’s all over at Elland Road, with Leeds and Man Utd playing out a competitive draw. Mbeumo’s opener was cancelled out by Calvert-Lewin’s equaliser in a game that was low on attacking quality and chances. Ultimately, a draw was a very fair reflection of the match. Man Utd are 14th and winless in six games across all competitions, while Leeds move into the top seven.

FULL-TIME: Dominic Calvert-Lewin earns a point for Leeds against Manchester United 💪 https://t.co/yDzLRE3Ir5

There are two yellow cards in quick succession as Ampadu is cautioned for a late tackle on Amad. Andrey Santos runs over and barges into the Leeds captain to earn himself a booking. The referee quickly calms then drama down.

Unconvincing goalkeeping from Lammens as he only punches Ampadu’s cross as far as Stach, whose tame shot squeezes through the Belgian’s legs. However, it’s blocked by the Man Utd defence and Lammens eventually gathers the ball.

There will be four minutes of added time. Can either side snatch a late victory?

Three times now United have looked like they’re about to get away down the flanks in the last few minutes and each time they’ve been flagged offside (Amad twice, Mbeumo once) and each occasion the player was able to look across the line. Carrick looked to the heavens. And he’s right to be frustrated. So avoidable.

Nmecha and Maguire challenge for the ball in the air, with the Man Utd defender bumping into the back of the Leeds substitute’s head. The crowd half-heartedly appeal for a penalty, but it’s quickly checked and cleared by VAR.

Carrick responds with a positive, attacking switch as Tielemans departs for Cunha.

Farke makes another change for Leeds as Longstaff replaces Tanaka in midfield.

Excellently goalkeeping from Trafford, who dashes out of his six-yard box to collect Andrey Santos’ pass and keep the ball in his grasp while staying in his box under the watchful eye of Mbeumo.

Dalot drives forward and leads a counter-attack. He passes to Amad, who forces a corner as Leeds get back well and recover. Man Utd take a clever short corner routine, but it ends with Mount scuffing an effort wide.

Both teams make changes. For Leeds, Nmecha replaces Okafor, while Mount enters the action for Man Utd as Baleba is withdrawn. The Englishman will sit alongside Andrey Santos in the away side’s midfield pivot.

From presentable range, Fernandes curls an effort straight into Trafford’s arms. Dalot then fails to adequately deal with a cross, heading the ball only as far as Stach. However, the Leeds midfielder wildly lashes his strike over the bar.

United were under that cosh in that period after Leeds equalised but they’ve gained a foothold back in the game now and a bit of frustration has crept in among the home fans. Stach the third player to fire high over the bar. Could go either way this.

How much longer will Carrick wait before making some changes in forward areas? His side need some renewed attacking impetus. The Man Utd head coach has Rashford, Cunha, Mount and Zirkzee all on the bench to choose from.

Okafor attempts to spearhead a Leeds break by playing in Calvert-Lewin. However, his pass is poor and it’s intercepted by Maguire. Amad is down after being caught by Tanaka earlier in that phase of play.

On the turn, Fernandes drags a low effort wide of the far post in a rare attacking flurry for Man Utd in this second half.

Ampadu feels Leeds should have a penalty as he collides with Maguire at a corner. The Man Utd defender hauls the Leeds captain to the floor. It’s been checked and cleared by VAR, but Maguire was taking a huge risk there.

Michael Carrick will surely be angry at the way Manchester United have started the second-half. One-nil up they have been far too slow and casual - highlighted by Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s goal which was embarrassingly easy to score from a corner. Leeds now on top and a huge few minutes ahead for Carrick.

Gudmundsson’s searching cross can’t quite find Calvert-Lewin as Man Utd scramble it clear. The away side’s backline has three defenders playing out of position, and they’ve been made to pay by Leeds’ leveller.

How will Man Utd cope with that setback? Leeds are putting them under serious pressure and have flown out of the blocks since the break as Tanaka volleys over from outside the penalty area.

The hosts finally have something to shout about at Elland Road! Leeds have a corner and Muharemovic beats Mazraoui to the delivery. The defender glances the ball to Calvert-Lewin, who holds off Mbeumo before smashing a close-range half-volley into the bottom corner. Elland Road goes wild and Leeds now have the momentum at the start of this second half.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalises for Leeds against Manchester United 👊 https://t.co/mnpyxZJKbm

It looks like a straight swap as Mazraoui slots in as a centre back, with Yoro continuing to deputise on the right.

We are back under way the second half. Martinez has been withdrawn at half-time, with Mazraoui on as his replacement, while Leeds are unchanged.

That is a really good half for Manchester United. More for the scoreline than the performance, although they have grown into the game after a sluggish start. Bryan Mbeumo’s goal will come as a huge relief to Michael Carrick. Leeds, in truth, have been a disappointment although they were denied the opening goal by Senne Lammens with a fine save. They needs to raise the tempo and the crowd. It is far too quiet. If Manchester United can hold on or build on this it will be a huge result for their under-pressure manager.

Carrick will be delighted with that first half. Man Utd have frustrated Leeds, defended valiantly and found the all-important breakthrough thanks to Mbeumo’s opener. Despite all the drama leading up to this game, Man Utd look really organised and unified, limiting Leeds to very little in forward areas.

Ahead at the break 👊🔴 https://t.co/rSSC8Pu4iG

There will be two minutes of added time. Can Man Utd protect their lead until the break?

Bogle drives into Man Utd’s box and squeezes a shot through a sea of bodies. However, it trickles into Lammens’ arms.

A big few minutes here for Manchester United. They need to see this half out. The goal has really steadied them but important they take that lead into the interval.

Calvert-Lewin attempts to latch onto Bogle’s clipped cross, but he directs it harmlessly wide.

Carrick’s game plan has worked perfectly so far. Man Utd soaked up the early pressure with their determined defending, before growing in confidence over the last 10 minutes. Mbeumo’s goal was much deserved.

You could see what that goal meant to Michael Carrick. He’s not one to show his emotions but he punches the air and wears the steely look of a man who knows how important it was to get the first goal here.

Mbeumo missed an earlier chance, but he makes no mistake with that one! Amad slips in Tielemans, who whips a magnificent cross into Mbeumo. The forward shows great composure and guides the delivery into the bottom corner.

Bryan Mbeumo finds the net this time to put Manchester United 1-0 up at Leeds! 🔴 https://t.co/NKDIhlUND1

The crowd loves that as Trafford sprints way out of his box almost to the halfway line to beat Amad to a ball over the top. Man Utd then make a promising break through Mbeumo, whose tame effort is easily gathered by Trafford.

Bogle attempts to take everyone on as he dribbles into Man Utd’s penalty area. He glides away from Dalot and Martinez, but overruns it, allowing Maguire to come across and shepherd the ball out of play.

Chants of “you soft southern b------” from the Leeds fans every time a Manchester United player goes down injured. Just a reminder that Leeds is actually only 22 miles further north than Manchester.

The away side are growing into this contest, with a slick move seeing Baleba find Dalot. The right back sprints into Leeds’ box, but he’s tackled well by Bogle.

Mbeumo misses a massive opportunity! Tielemans clips in a cross and an unmarked Mbeumo finds space between Elvedi and Muharemovic but heads wide. He has to get that on target.

Bryan Mbeumo comes close to giving Manchester United the lead 😬 https://t.co/j5PFXa2Uhe

Leeds test Lammens! Stach whips in a free kick, which is met by Elvedi, whose downward header is parried away by Lammens. That’s Leeds’ best chance so far, but the Man Utd goalkeeper did his job.

Leeds have enjoyed nearly 70% possession, but they’re yet to have a shot of any note. That’s testament to Man Utd’s competitiveness and organisation. Bogle then digs out a promising cross, but Yoro heads it away at the back post.

In fairness to Man Utd, they’re defending solidly and doing well to frustrate Leeds. Gudmundsson is then carded for catching Andrey Santos on his ankle with a very unpleasant challenge. It’s been such a physical and scruffy match so far.

Risky from Fernandes as he lunges in with a dangerous challenge on Muharemovic. Leeds then break as Martinez misses his tackle on Calvert-Lewin, but Stach’s cross is blocked. When the ball eventually goes out of play, Fernandes is booked for that earlier challenge. He can have no complaints.

United staff aggrieved that Fernandes should be booked but Ampadu escape a yellow card before then for arguably a worse challenge on Mbeumo, whom he caught thick on the ankle with his studs.

🫡 Ethan Ampadu starts as captain for the 100th time, becoming the youngest player to reach that milestone since Billy Bremner! https://t.co/80YrU08S3s

No early rhythm in this game so far. It’s still a little frantic at the moment, with Leeds having most of the ball and trying to force the issue.

Leeds crunch into a couple of heavy challenges on the Man Utd players in these early exchanges. Stach is eventually penalised for a strong tackle, but it’s a purposeful start from the hosts.

Interestingly, it looks like Fernandes is starting centrally in the ‘false nine’ position, with Mbeumo and Amad out on the wings. The Man Utd captain started out wide in Spain on Wednesday - an experiment that definitely did not work.

We are under way at Elland. Can Leeds pile more misery on Man Utd or will the visitors answer their critics with a much-needed win?

Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin was the only player not to take the knee prior to kick-off for the Premier League’s ‘No Room for Racism’ campaign. The gesture from the other players was roundly booed by a lot of the fans inside Elland Road.

Both teams are out on the pitch, with kick-off fast approaching.

There have been wide open spaces in Manchester United’s side for opponents to exploit this season so it’s no surprise to see Michael Carrick keep faith with an extra body in midfield. It could make for a rather disjointed set up.

Lisandro Martinez keeps his place despite his rant at the Old Trafford board in midweek but the bigger concern has been his individual performances this season - they have been nowhere near good enough and he’s brought extra scrutiny on himself with the tirade. Bruno Fernandes is going to have to operate out wide you would think if Youri Tielemans plays centrally ahead of Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos.

Leeds are the kind of compact, organised, aggressive in-your-face team United have tended to struggle against in recent years. They were good in defeat to Arsenal last weekend and showcased their considerable threat in the 4-1 win over Newcastle. Expect a white-hot atmosphere at Elland Road. They cannot stand Manchester United in these parts.

Lisandro Martínez delivered a strong and powerful message to his Manchester United team-mates: if you’re playing terribly, use the director of football as a punchbag and you might become a hero.

It is a popular play in a world in which certain players have become as adept at scapegoat-hunting as man-marking. Passionately speak about what someone else at your football club is doing wrong – particularly the unloved executives – and cast yourself as a whistleblower, selflessly exposing the truth that the long-suffering supporters deserve.

Such internal fights make for great drama, unless your own club is caught in the middle of it.

That’s why in the immediate aftermath of Martínez’s scathing comments about Jason Wilcox following the Champions League defeat by Atlético Madrid, there was a division between those who celebrated the Argentine speaking out and those who felt it was self-serving, a convenient deflection by an out-of-form player in the final year of his contract.

The narrative is completely dominated by the drama around Man Utd, which should suit Leeds perfectly. All eyes and pressure is on their opponents, and they have every reason to feel confident ahead of this huge clash at Elland Road.

Kobbie Mainoo is also sidelined, while Matheus Cunha and Marcus Rashford are benched. The big news is that Lisandro Martinez starts for the visitors, despite his scathing outburst earlier in the week. Just 10 months on from Ruben Amorim’s final game in charge of Manchester United, the club return to Elland Road on Sunday afternoon with another manager under pressure and the director of football again in the spotlight.

The difference is Michael Carrick still has a chance to determine the course of his United future whereas Amorim had already sealed his fate after a furious bust-up with Jason Wilcox 48 hours before his last game ended in a 1-1 draw with Leeds and post-match fireworks.

But even for a club never far from a crisis, it seems remarkable to think they are back in a tailspin so soon after Amorim’s sacking in early January.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Leeds United at Elland Road.

Quiet week in the world of Man Utd? Don’t be silly. Following a 2-0 defeat in the Champions League against Atlético Madrid in Spain on Wednesday, defender Lisandro Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on Man Utd’s director of football Jason Wilcox and the club’s hierarchy because of a dreadful start to the campaign, which has yielded two victories in nine games across all competitions.

The Argentine criticised Man Utd’s recruitment and said he expected more, but didn’t suggest Carrick was to blame. Martinez has since apologised for his outburst and met with Wilcox, Man Utd chief executive Omar Berrada and Michael Carrick, with Telegraph Sport understanding that he’s free to play today, although his role remains unclear as we all eagerly await the team news.

Carrick is under immense pressure to get a result here in Yorkshire, with last weekend’s 1-1 draw with 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford condemning Man Utd to their worst league start for 40 years.

With all eyes on the visitors, Leeds will be licking their lips at the prospect of piling further misery on their beleaguered opponents. Daniel Farke’s side suffered their first Premier League loss last weekend, falling 2-1 to Arsenal at the Emirates after going a goal up, but the mood remains positive after a solid start to the campaign.

Leeds are eighth and the club will be harbouring ambitions of a top-half finish in the Premier League for the first time since the 2019/20 season, with the prospect of qualifying for European football not out of the realm of possibility.

Unlike Man Utd, Leeds have a settled, reliable system that clearly suits their current squad. Elland Road will also be a cauldron of hostility and noise, given the fierce backdrop between these two bitter rivals.

This has all the ingredients to be a thrilling and fascinating watch as we bring you the latest updates, information and drama. Kick-off is at 14:00, with team news coming shortly.

#1368. Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock reveals he hid seizures from club because he was 'petrified' of being released as youngster

Published: 19:09 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 19:15 EDT, 1 November 2026

Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock has revealed he hid seizures from the club out of fear that the Reds would axe him.

Warnock, 44, played 67 times for Liverpool and has transitioned into broadcasting since retiring from playing in 2018.

He suffered from a number of epileptic fits as a youngster - a condition that affects around one in every 100 people.

Warnock never understood what was causing his seizures and told 5 Live: 'I was petrified of telling Liverpool because I was worried about being released. Because I was thinking "if they think I've got a condition they will release me".

'I was worried about being on the pitch and it happens. There were no triggers for me, I never knew what triggered it. That was what petrified me.'

Warnock experienced the seizures for around three years and underwent a number of tests including a CT and MRI scan.

Stephen Warnock, pictured working as a broadcaster, revealed he suffered from seizures

The former Liverpool defender, pictured in action for the Reds back in 2005, said he was terrified of telling the club about his health issue

'I was at a computer and then I woke up in a hospital bed,' he went on. 'And I was like "wow, how have I got here?". I didn't remember anything, I completely blacked out.

'My friends told me I started having a seizure. Obviously an ambulance was called and I was taken to a hospital bed.

'I was embarrassed to be honest, because no-one else had it, no-one knew about it, I didn't know about it until it happened.'

The risk of having a seizure can be reduced with medication and Warnock has not experienced one since he was 14.

'I was in a fortunate position where I grew out of it,' he said.

'I didn't have to go on medication or worry about driving a car or things like that. It's the first time I've ever really spoken about it.'

Warnock, a left-back, departed Liverpool in 2007 and went on to play for Aston Villa, Leeds and Derby among other sides.

He has appeared on a number of television channels while working as a pundit, including the BBC, Sky Sports, BT Sport, NBC and DAZN.

#1367. Invincibles beware! Mikel Arteta might just be assembling Arsenal's greatest EVER defence, writes ISAAN KHAN

Published: 21:00 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 03:48 EDT, 2 November 2026

Within seconds of the full-time whistle, Gabriel Heinze had lifted an elated Mikel Arteta off the turf.

The Argentine knew why this result brought his colleague a certain catharsis, which had eluded him for over a decade.

Arteta had previously opened up about the psychological difficulties of playing at Anfield, describing the experience akin to a cyclist suddenly running out of energy. A mental paralysis of sorts.

The game in question was in February 2014, having experienced a 5-1 defeat as a Gunners player. Arsenal’s previous victory against Liverpool away dated back to September 2012, a 14-year wait to banish these demons which he was duly reminded of in Friday’s press conference and in the minutes before kick-off.

Instead, it’s now getting scary for Arsenal’s Premier League title rivals. The prospect of Arteta's side opening up a gap from the chasing pack by Christmas is becoming a real possibility — and it’s all because of their defence.

A William Saliba-less backline reducing the Reds to zero shots on target at Anfield is a moment worth digesting.

Mikel Arteta and Gabriel Heinze jubilantly embrace as the final whistle blows at Anfield

Arsenal ended their 14-year wait for a Premier League victory at Anfield with a superb display

Winning on opposition territory after an abysmal record lasting over a decade is an achievement in itself. But to ensure a frontline featuring Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola aren't given so much as a sniff in front of goal is a further statement.

For all the focus around the fragilities of their frontline — the weaknesses are still very much in the open, as seen by the shock Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood Town — it’s Arsenal’s defence which underpins everything.

Since the start of last season, Arsenal have not lost a league game when leading the scoreline at half-time. Just like how Arsenal’s (previously) woeful record at Anfield would be used as a reminder, this statistic is a menacing one for future opponents.

It raises the question: how does this backline compare to the best Premier League defences who came before them?

If the team carry on in this vein towards a consecutive league title, the Arsenal Invincibles set-up from the historic 2003-04 season of Sol Campbell, Kolo Toure, Ashley Cole and Lauren, with Jens Lehmann in goal, could soon be superseded.

The current collection of defenders, backed up by David Raya, create a defensive structure which is proving so hard to break down, even with the lack of a sole regular scorer in the side.

Gabriel, despite his embarrassing attempt at pretending Isak struck him in the face yesterday, stayed strong in physical duels and didn’t relent in periods when Liverpool piled the pressure on.

By the 42nd minute, the Reds had whipped in 17 crosses, many of which were cleared by Gabriel or Konsa.

Riccardo Calafiori is a wonderfully-gifted footballer who finds himself in some unorthodox positions which are difficult to track. The Italian’s menacing runs inverting from the left flank caused Liverpool many a problem.

Kai Havertz tapped home from a low cross early on to give Arsenal a crucial lead to defend

Even Jurrien Timber, who didn’t have his best game in the final third, helped ensure solidity at right back up against Cody Gakpo.

It’s Ezri Konsa, though, who reflects a shrewdness typifying Arsenal and Arteta. As soon as it emerged that Saliba would be sidelined for months with a back injury, a right-sided centre back became the priority.

The 29-year-old has slotted in seamlessly and again shone against the Reds, mirroring the ‘blessed’ tattoo he has inscribed on his left hand.

The versatile defender won 100 per cent of his ground duels, made 14 defensive contributions and completed eight clearances. He ranked No1 in all these categories yesterday.

An Arteta team starts from a rock-solid base with multiple, versatile defenders, often at the cost of fewer frontline options (Arsenal struck just two more league goals than third-placed Manchester United last season, for example).

It ultimately worked in the previous campaign, their defence propelling Arsenal to a first Premier League title in 22 years.

Another title appears to be well on track. And: watch out Campbell and Co. The moniker for Arsenal’s best defence in modern history is at risk.

GUNNERS GAINING FROM MIKEL'S RUTHLESS STREAK

Arteta’s ruthlessness is well-documented. Just ask Aaron Ramsdale or Jakub Kiwior, who were eased out after being surplus to requirements in recent years.

Or the cold treatment of Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Mesut Ozil earlier in the Spaniard’s reign over their behaviours.

Arteta's ruthlessness with team selection is continuing to pay dividends for the Gunners

The current squad is brimming with talent — and spades of uncertainty.

Eberechi Eze performed well off the bench against Bayern Munich after Bukayo Saka’s thigh injury on 10 minutes, followed up by a start against Everton — and didn’t get a minute against Liverpool.

While Viktor Gyokeres was given his first league start of the season against Everton, where he played well — only to be dropped for this match.

As seen by Christos Tzolis’ dash to make yesterday’s squad ahead of schedule, influenced by Max Dowman’s three-match suspension, no one’s place is really secure.

That makes for a truly competitive environment.

The fiery serial-winner, drafted in by Arteta in July 2025, was always going to demand high standards and bring a ferocity which can turn some the wrong way. At Argentine side Newell’s Old Boys, for example, he would weigh the players twice a day.

Heinze's arrival in July 2025 has added a steeliness to the defence and paid off in spades

So the appointment was attached with risks, even if Arteta had grown close to his ex-team-mate from his Paris Saint-Germain.

It’s turned out to be a clever addition, which has added a steeliness to the defence and paid off in spades.

Sources say that Heinze, who has managed five teams, is well-respected by the players, but is also seen as someone who does not mince his words. They know he’s not here to mess around.

#1366. Molecular underpinnings of rheumatic diseases and emerging therapeutic concepts

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature volume 658, pages 1141–1152 (2026) Cite this article

Inflammatory rheumatic diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus represent chronic inflammatory disorders that are caused by dysregulation of innate and adaptive immune responses. Here we review current advances in our understanding of the molecular underpinnings of these diseases and discuss consequences with respect to emerging targets and treatment strategies, which are increasingly enabling more robust disease control and the first prospects of a cure for previously chronic inflammatory rheumatic diseases.

Kai Havertz made Premier League history in the perfect setting, scoring Arsenal’s winning goal at Anfield while becoming the highest-scoring German player the competition has ever seen.

The 27-year-old struck after just 16 minutes to secure Arsenal’s 1-0 victory over Liverpool, ending the Gunners’ 14-year wait for a Premier League win at Anfield.

More significantly on a personal level, the goal took Havertz to 46 Premier League strikes, moving him clear of former Manchester City midfielder İlkay Gündoğan.

Havertz’s simple back-post finish made history, with Declan Rice providing the decisive delivery.

Opta confirmed that Havertz is now the Premier League’s all-time leading German goalscorer with 46 goals, surpassing Gündoğan’s previous record of 45.

Of those goals, 19 came during his time at Chelsea and 27 have now been scored for Arsenal. His Anfield winner was also his third Premier League goal of the current season.

Kai Havertz is now the top German-scorer in Premier League history 😤🇩🇪 https://t.co/lWpXBt0sI5

— Prime Video Sport UK (@primevideosport) November 1, 2026

The occasion made the record even more memorable. Arsenal had not won a league game at Anfield since September 2012, but Havertz’s early finish proved enough to send Mikel Arteta’s side back to the top of the Premier League, three points ahead of Manchester City.

Arsenal punished Alisson Becker’s costly distribution error before Havertz finished the move.

Kai Havertz gives Arsenal an early lead at Anfield! ⚡️ https://t.co/eeyhRcLlel

— Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) November 1, 2026

Havertz’s Arsenal career has often been debated, but milestones like this show just how productive he has become.

He is not always the most spectacular forward, and his finishing can still frustrate, but 46 Premier League goals is a major achievement considering he has spent significant periods playing in midfield rather than as a conventional striker.

Arteta selected Havertz ahead of Viktor Gyökeres for one of Arsenal’s biggest away games of the season, and he repaid that faith with the decisive moment.

Breaking Gündoğan’s record at Anfield while ending Arsenal’s long winless run there makes the achievement even more significant.

Havertz may still divide opinion, but statistically he now stands above every other German goalscorer in Premier League history and at 27, he has plenty of time to extend that record further.

#1364. 'I have something unresolved': Ole Gunnar Solskjaer piles more pressure on old pal Michael Carrick as he says he WOULD manage Man United again - despite trying to back him to succeed

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 03:52 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 05:42 EDT, 2 November 2026

Ole Gunnar Solskjaer has admitted that he would be interested in returning as Manchester United manager in the future as he has 'something unresolved'.

Pressure is mounting on current head coach Michael Carrick as the Red Devils' dismal season continues to go from bad to worse.

After losing 2-0 at Chelsea on Saturday afternoon, United sit 17th in the Premier League - only above 18th-placed Crystal Palace on goal difference and just two points ahead of bottom side Sunderland.

Solskjaer has been in the Old Trafford hotseat before with his own path mirroring Carrick's from being an interim manager initially to becoming a permanent appointment.

The Norwegian had Carrick among his backroom staff before he was sacked as United boss in November 2021. When Ruben Amorim was sacked in January, both were interviewed as interim successors before Carrick was chosen.

And speaking about taking the reins at United in the future, Solskjaer revealed he would accept it.

Ole Gunnar Solskjaer (left) has revealed he would like to manage Manchester United in the future but backs current head coach Michael Carrick (right) to overturn the club's fortunes

Pressure is growing on Carrick which increased following Saturday's 2-0 defeat at Chelsea

Solskjaer was sacked as United manager in November 2021 after nearly three years in charge

'Going back to what has been is not always as good,' he told Norwegian outfit TV2.

'Yes, I had lined up [as Manchester United's interim manager last season], but I didn't think it would last longer than the summer. It was probably time for someone else to try.

'I also feel like I have something unresolved. Of course it would have been nice to have the opportunity again.'

Elaborating further, Solskjaer was keen to stress that he is not looking to oust his former United team-mate and friend Carrick.

'If Michael does well for 10 years and decides to quit, and they ask me if I can take them for two months, of course I wouldn't say no. I've been at that club for 18-19 years, so it's part of the family. But it's not something I'm thinking about.'

Despite growing scrutiny on Carrick, Solskjaer is adamant that the under-fire head coach can turn around the club's fortunes.

'Michael has what it takes to take that club forward. I think he's the right man. He understands the club, understands the fans and knows what's needed.'

Proof will be in the pudding with Carrick preparing his side for Tuesday's Champions League clash with Roma and then Sunday's Premier League encounter versus Aston Villa, both at Old Trafford, before the international break.

Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard has delivered a surprising verdict on Trent Alexander-Arnold’s potential return to Anfield, admitting that he is unsure whether re-signing the defender would be the right decision for Andoni Iraola’s squad.

The former Liverpool captain believes Alexander-Arnold possesses the quality to improve the Reds, but has questioned whether bringing him back would benefit the current group following his controversial departure to Real Madrid.

Alexander-Arnold has been linked with a sensational return to Merseyside after struggling to establish himself as a regular starter at the Santiago Bernabéu.

However, Gerrard believes the circumstances surrounding the England international’s departure could complicate any potential reunion.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, Gerrard was asked directly whether he would welcome Trent Alexander-Arnold back to Liverpool.

The former Reds captain admitted that he would personally support the move, pointing towards the defender’s exceptional ability and achievements at Anfield.

However, he also acknowledged that the manner of Alexander-Arnold’s departure remains a sensitive subject.

“Ability and talent-wise, the success he’s had, I would say yes. But the ending and that still being a bit raw. I would, yes, myself personally, so I won’t sit on the fence because that’s poor from me.

“Do I think it’s the right thing for this group, this manager and where Liverpool are right now? I’m unsure. Does he make Liverpool’s team and squad better? Ability and talent-wise, 100 per cent. I’m just not sure it’s right for the group right now.”

Steven Gerrard on whether he’d take Trent Alexander-Arnold back at Liverpool.

Watch the latest Overlap Daily episode at 4pm on YouTube or listen wherever you get your podcasts ??? pic.twitter.com/GC1W5EfnMx

— Overlap Daily (@ThatsFootballTV) November 2, 2026

While he remains convinced of Alexander-Arnold’s footballing ability, he is less certain about the impact his return could have on the current dressing room.

The former captain’s assessment is particularly notable given his close association with Liverpool and his understanding of the expectations surrounding players at Anfield.

Alexander-Arnold’s future has become a subject of growing speculation following his move to Real Madrid.

The 28-year-old left Liverpool after spending his entire senior career at Anfield, having progressed through the club’s academy to become one of its most influential players.

His departure proved controversial among Liverpool supporters, particularly given the manner of his exit that left a sour taste among the fanbase.

However, the England international has struggled to secure a regular starting position in Madrid.

Having found himself down the pecking order in Madrid, rumors have intensified of a potential early exit and that Liverpool could explore an ambitious move to bring the England international back home.

Alexander-Arnold’s creativity, passing range and ability to dictate play from right-back would undoubtedly offer improve Liverpool’s right side, specially given that they currently do not have a top-class right-back.

Ronald Araujo has done a remarkable job filling in as a right-back since joining the club on loan from Barcelona but his strongest position remains a centre-back.

And despite Gerrard’s claims, him returning may not have an impact on the dressing room as many players who played with him during his time at the club will likely welcome him back.

That said, the supporters may not be as forgiving, with many on social media already against the idea of bringing him back regardless of the quality he brings.

#1362. Liverpool's anonymous attackers cost them the chance of beating Arsenal despite dominant display... the gap to the champions is narrowing - but the Reds still aren't close enough, writes LEWIS STEELE

Published: 21:00 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 06:06 EDT, 2 November 2026

As disheartened fans spilled out of Anfield, nearly all conversations were about the referee and questions over why he did not point to the penalty spot in the first half when Jurrien Timber pulled back Alexander Isak.

They had a point and this game would have been completely different had Andy Madley – or VAR Stuart Attwell – seen what everyone else saw when Isak was an inch short of connecting with a header and possible goal because he was pulled back by his marker.

It was a similar situation to Liverpool’s only other defeat under new boss Andoni Iraola, where supporters were left aggrieved at the incorrect call to send off Ryan Gravenberch against Manchester City.

In both cases they were unlucky to be on the wrong side of refereeing mistakes and would have cursed the fine margins. But in both cases Reds fans will also realise their team just did not do enough to win too.

Just like against City, Liverpool dominated Arsenal for large parts of this match. It felt as though they were one magic moment or opposition mistake away from scoring and lfiting off the Anfield roof.

But in both cases, that moment never materialised. It felt like the Liverpool attackers were looking around waiting for somebody else to step up and be the man to start the pendulum swinging in Liverpool’s favour.

Alexander Isak and Liverpool's attackers struggled against Arsenal's defence

They had zero shots on target, according to Opta, and that is the only statistic that Iraola will be mulling over in the coming days.

Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have all been frighteningly good in recent weeks but in this game, especially the second half, Liverpool’s big-money forwards looked like they had run out of ideas.

Arsenal defended like their lives depended on it and their away fans, who barely saw the ball down their end of the pitch after half-time, celebrated every Gabriel header or David Raya catch like a goal.

The home team, meanwhile, were left throwing long balls forward to Virgil van Dijk – the only player who could aerially compete with Arsenal’s team of giants. It felt like several Hail Mary passes but no one could answer Iraola’s prayers.

Liverpool’s two defeats to City and now Arsenal both demonstrate the gap between Iraola’s outfit and a genuine title contender. There is definitely a small level between Liverpool and Arsenal – but Reds fans can take solace in knowing it is not a chasm like last season.

A referee decision here, a better final ball there and Liverpool may be still unbeaten under Iraola and the whole country would consider them a title contender.

Iraola has closed the gap on the top teams but knows several tweaks are still needed to take that next step. Can they do it this season? It is far from impossible but seems a tall order.

The upcoming fixture list is kinder to them, at least. Of the current top eight, Liverpool have played all of them – two in the Carabao Cup – and won each test apart from City and Arsenal. The next two league games are against teams in 18th and 17th.

Florian Wirtz has improved recently but was unable to provide cutting edge on Sunday

But right now, Liverpool are a team with too many ‘ifs’, ‘buts’ and ‘maybes’. If Alexis Mac Allister did not get under a first-half header that looked like a certain goal… if the referee had given a clear foul on Isak… if the forwards packed their shooting boots.

As it was, for all of the nail-biting moments for Mikel Arteta on the touchline as Liverpool had lots of the ball in the final third, his goalkeeper David Raya could have had a cigar in and read the papers for most of the second half.

That is what will bother Iraola the most.

As for being a complete team able to compete for the league title again, Liverpool seem so close yet so far.

Trey Nyoni made his first Premier League start and it will not be his last after he put in a solid shift.

Though he misplaced some passes and was probably lucky to escape an early yellow card after two late challenges, the 19-year-old presents Iraola with an interesting tactical quirk.

The Englishman always wants the ball and drops into the back line to start attacks, with a maturity beyond his years.

He sits deep which allows Alexis Mac Allister to play as more of a box-to-box midfielder, undoubtedly his best position.

So where does this leave Ryan Gravenberch, who spent the afternoon on the bench? Given the amount of games Liverpool have across competitions, the Dutchman will still play many minutes — but he is currently at risk of falling down the pecking order thanks to the exciting talent of Nyoni.

There is also a conversation to be had about how Liverpool’s balance and control was lost when Nyoni was replaced by Dominik Szoboszlai.

Trey Nyoni excelled for the Reds and helped the home side control the tempo

Casual football fans who maybe only tune in for the big games have never seen Wirtz play well.

They must wonder what all the fuss is about.

The German has been on fine form in recent weeks but has been like a ghost — no Halloween pun intended — in the two biggest matches against City and Arsenal.

It is all well and good performing against teams like LASK in the Champions League but Wirtz, at £116million, was signed to make a difference in these blockbuster clashes.

Instead, his national team colleague Kai Havertz continued his record of impacting the games that really matter come May. How Wirtz could do with some of that killer instinct.

READ: Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal PLAYER RATINGS: Whose touch let him down? Who produced another promising display after facing scrutiny? And how did youngster Trey Nyoni settle in?

Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard has heaped praise on Tottenham Hotspur youngster Luca Williams-Barnett following his impressive cameo against Crystal Palace, comparing the 18-year-old to Liverpool’s highly rated winger Rio Ngumoha.

The attacking midfielder came off the bench during Tottenham’s 2-0 Premier League victory over Palace at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, catching Gerrard’s attention with an exciting piece of individual skill.

Despite playing only around ten minutes, Williams-Barnett made a strong impression on the former England captain, who believes Spurs have an exceptional young talent on their hands.

Gerrard was particularly impressed by the teenager’s confidence in possession and his willingness to take on defenders.

Speaking on The Overlap, Gerrard revealed that he had already heard positive reports about Williams-Barnett through England’s youth setup.

However, it was the youngster’s performance against Crystal Palace that convinced him Tottenham have a player worth watching closely. He said:

“I loved one moment from the game. Williams-Barnett, a name I’ve heard mentioned to me through the England ranks a few times.

“But he came on for a little cameo, and if I’m a Tottenham fan, I’m going away buzzing with the result, and Spurs are obviously in this new place, but this young kid is going to be a player.

“I’ve seen enough in the 10-minute cameo. He came on around the 80th minute; he went on this little jinky run down the left and put a ball across like Declan Rice.

“I just thought, ‘They’ve got their own little Rio Ngumoha’. So look out for this boy, I really like him.”

Comparing the Spurs starlet to Liverpool’s breakout winger Rio Ngumoha, Gerrard highlighted the teenager’s fearlessness and elite technical quality when taking on defenders under pressure.

Williams-Barnett has already established himself as one of Tottenham’s most promising academy prospects.

The attacking midfielder signed his first professional contract with Spurs after turning 17 and has continued to attract attention through his performances at youth level.

One of his most eye-catching achievements came in the UEFA Youth League, where he scored five goals in a single match last season.

His rapid development in North London has not gone unnoticed by Europe’s elite. European heavyweights Bayern Munich, alongside Premier League rivals Chelsea and Manchester United, have actively tracked his progress.

That interest reflects the reputation Williams-Barnett has built as an exciting attacking talent capable of operating in different positions.

The youngster’s technical ability, close control and confidence in one-on-one situations make him an intriguing option for Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi.

Under Roberto De Zerbi, Williams-Barnett is now making his mark on Tottenham’s first team, giving Spurs fans reason to celebrate a generational talent in their ranks.

And new reports suggest that Spurs are trying hard to secure a new long-term agreement with the starlet.

With other clubs reportedly monitoring his progress, retaining one of their brightest academy talents could become an important priority for Spurs.

#1360. Narrow carbon pentaheptite nanoribbon as a covalent metal

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature volume 658, pages 1176–1182 (2026) Cite this article

Metallic carbon-based nanoribbons are sought after1,2 as atomically defined one-dimensional conductors with potential relevance to future carbon-based electrodes and interconnects3, ideally with quantum-limited conductance comparable to metallic carbon nanotubes4. Metallic graphene nanoribbons have been realized by band engineering, notably through zero-mode superlattices1. However, atomically precise metallic nanoribbons of fully non-benzenoid carbon allotropes, such as the theorized metallic carbon pentaheptites5,6, remain unexplored. The realization of these nanoribbons could enable bottom-up fabrication of all-carbon electronics7,8 compatible with semiconducting graphene nanoribbons9,10,11,12,13 and nanographenes14,15, along with their fascinating properties16,17,18,19,20. Here we report a hierarchical approach for the on-surface synthesis of planar carbon pentaheptite nanoribbons (CPHNs) by laterally fusing well-aligned polypentalene chains transformed from pre-synthesized polycyclooctadiene chains. Two distinct types of narrow pentaheptite nanoribbon share a similar basal structure consisting of a central heptagon chain flanked by either identically (CPHN 1) or differently (CPHN 2) oriented polypentalene chains on opposite lateral edges. CPHN 1 is an intrinsic metal, whereas CPHN 2 is a narrow-bandgap semiconductor. The CPHN 1 ribbon exhibits near-ballistic conductance approaching one conductance quantum, comparable to metallic carbon nanotubes4. This highlights CPHN 1 as a promising planar carbon metal and suggests a possible route towards carbon quantum wires, although further synthetic optimization will be required for device integration.

A smaller energy broadening is applied in panels f,i than in Fig. 4n to resolve the two closely spaced peaks near Fermi energy. Different termini used show an obvious effect in the positions of band B1 minimum, even with the similar length of freestanding CPHN 1.

a−c, Chemical structures of wide [3]CPHNs composed of three fused PPTLs with different orientations (marked with black lines at right side). d−f, DFT-calculated band structures of the [3]CPHNs in a−c, respectively. g, Large-scale STM topographic image of Br-decoupled [3]CPHN on Ag(111). h,i, Zoom-in STM topographic image and nc-AFM image taken within the marked frame in g. j, Derived chemical structure of the [3]CPHN segment according to the AFM image, showing the structure in type 2 consisting of three fused PPTLs with alternatively altered orientations. k, Normalized 2D LDOS map recorded along the arrowed line grids in panel h with equidistant 128 points. l, FT-LDOS pattern from the map in k, shown within the Brillouin zone \(0 < k < \frac{\pi }{a}\). The minimum of band B1 is fitted to be positioned at −0.22 eV. m, Constant-height dI/dV maps of the [3]CPHN in h recorded at indicated bias voltages. Energy-dependent standing waves were observed like CPHN 1 and 2. All the STM, nc-AFM images and dI/dV maps are recorded with CO-functionalized tips. Tunneling parameters: g,h, −1.0 V, 20 pA; i, z-offset = 0 nm with respect to STM setpoint of −13 mV, 20 pA; m, STM setpoint at indicated bias and tunneling current of 500 pA.

#1359. Pioli: ‘Milan have four or five top players, Leao needs to be encouraged in a certain way’

Stefano Pioli believes that Milan currently have ‘four or five’ top-class players and has explained how he used to get the best out of former Rossoneri star Rafael Leao: ‘He has incredible quality.”

Pioli discussed his time with Milan in an appearance on Sky Sport Italia during Sunday’s Serie A match between Juventus and Napoli.

The 2021-22 Scudetto winner has been out of work since leaving Fiorentina early into the 2025-26 season, but says that a sabbatical has been exactly what he needed.

“I’m fine but I do miss it. I needed to take a break,” said Pioli.

“I really wanted to succeed with Fiorentina, I had other offers from abroad, but I didn’t take them into consideration. I think I made a mistake by trying to raise the bar too much. I put pressure on a team when there wasn’t a need to. Some results could have gone differently, but the pressure didn’t allow us to express ourselves properly.”

Pioli would go on to discuss his time with Milan and his relationship with Leao, who was sold to Galatasaray for a fee of just €38m over the summer, not including bonuses and sell-on clauses.

Leao was one of Milan’s star players when they last won the Scudetto and was also named as the division’s MVP that year.

“He was devastating in the year of the Scudetto, I’ve rarely seen players like that,” Pioli recalled.

“The work that Maldini, Massara and I did with him was important, he has incredible quality, but we weren’t as good at raising the bar for him, though.

“A coach has to understand his players. Rafa is a good player and a good person on the inside, but needs to be encouraged in a certain way. We had Kessie and Tonali, who did the job of three or four players. It’s not that Rafa can’t mark a full-back, it’s that he wasn’t supposed to. He would follow a centre-back and a midfielder would go wide. You need to find the right place for him.”

Pioli feels that current Milan star Diego Moreira has a bit of the Leao factor about him. He also went on to discuss Milan’s current squad and their need for more strength in depth.

“I watched him against Sassuolo and he impressed me. He and Rabiot have been very important players. Maignan made a great save [against Inter]. They’re a really strong team with their top 11 players, but they started to struggle a bit more when Amorim made a few more changes.

“It’s taken them a while to get to this point because when certain players arrived, they probably arrived with a few issues and needed time to settle in and find their rhythm. Now we’re seeing the results.

“Luka Modric is still an important player, Goncalo Ramos is doing a great job for the team as well.”

On Maignan, one of the few surviving Milan players from their 2021-22 Scudetto victory, Pioli said: “He’s the best in an absolute sense: The way he participates in games and the saves that he makes. Milan have four of five top players. Modric still has the legs in him, Rabiot, Pavlovic is a top defender, De Winter is growing as well. Ramos is an excellent striker and you can’t look past Pulisic either.”

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.
